items.title: Welcome to the Western Force
items.text:
The Western Force have been Western Australia’s Super Rugby team since 2006. The black and gold come from the state’s traditional colours.

After time outside the competition, the Force returned to Super Rugby in 2020. Home games are at HBF Park in Perth.

items.title: From the local club to Super Rugby
items.text:
Every player in the Western Force squad started at a local club. Talented juniors are picked for representative age-group teams, and the best join the club’s academy.

The academy adds coaching, strength and conditioning, and support with school or work, so players are ready when their chance comes.

image.alt: Perth city beside the Swan River

body.text: After time outside the competition, the Force returned to Super Rugby in 2020. Home games are at HBF Park in Perth.
In 2027 Perth hosts the opening match of the Rugby World Cup.
2006: The club plays its first Super Rugby season. 2020: Back in Super Rugby, in Super Rugby AU. 2027: Perth hosts the opening match of the Rugby World Cup.

data.headline: Match day at HBF Park: what to know
data.standfirst: Tickets, getting there and what to expect at a home game.

image.alt: Rugby stadium with goalposts and spectators in the stands

body.text: Home games at HBF Park are a day out for the whole family. Here is how to plan yours.
Members keep the same seat all season. Single tickets go on sale before each game, and children’s tickets are discounted.
Public transport is the easiest way to HBF Park on game day. Allow extra time: the roads around the ground are busy before kick-off.
Gates open well before kick-off, with activities for kids on the concourse. Stay after the game for signing sessions on selected dates.

data.headline: Inside the academy: from club rugby to Super Rugby
data.standfirst: How young players in Western Australia find their way into the Western Force squad.

image.alt: A coach giving instructions to a young player at training

body.text: Every player in the Western Force squad started at a local club. The academy is the bridge between club rugby and the professional game.
Talented juniors are spotted in club and school rugby and in representative age-group teams, then invited to train with the academy.
Coaching, strength and conditioning, and support with school or work, so players are ready when their chance comes.
The same pathway leads to the club’s Super W team.
